method: Read all eight round-2 A/B sheets and the tree look-dev. Recaptured on the current tree: max_env_shots --tag max2_vq1 (rift core, jungle_w, xi, jungle_e, outflow, jungle_s; bridge base, deck; High, t=20, 28.5 m) against maxenv/max2_before, with 1:1 crops of the jungle_w floor, the outflow mouth and the bridge deck. Also ran shot_structures rift for damage (vq1_struct_damage33/66) and collapse plus ruin (vq1b_struct_*). I restored the tracked structures_rift.json report. I checked frame value stats with numpy. There is no audio in this lane.

items.evidence: Recapture max2_vq1/rift_jungle_e.png: the Serenade east now reads as two species at the game camera. Lampbough has star-cut warm crowns on tall bare boles among the round Dialwood fans. rift_jungle_s.png and rift_xi.png show Hourtier as a cooler sage-teal tiered crown, and in xi all three species sit in one frame. This closes the round-1 'one species' gap, the main reason verify2 held 7.4. Residuals: Lampbough reads amber only in sun (xi); in shadow (jungle_e) it goes rust-brown and reads as a withered or autumn tree. Top-down, Hourtier is mostly a hue change on a similar rounded crown, and its pagoda tiers read only in sun (jungle_s). In shadow (jungle_w centre) it is a slate blob with a dark trunk hole.

1:1 crop of max2_vq1/rift_jungle_w.png (x 560-1560, y 500-1080). Leaf-drift speckle is visible, but the clearing still reads as dark moss: frame mean 35.5 -> 36.0, p99 unchanged at 96. The dial-stone slabs and dapple pools show as hard-rimmed translucent pale ellipses: two in the jungle_w clearing, and one by the VII ruin in jungle_s (crop x 600-1000, y 330-560, a cool grey oval). They read as decal stains, not as sun pools or stones.

Crop of max2_vq1/rift_outflow.png vs max2_before (x 620-1220, y 420-900): the fall now reads as a pale comb of uneven streaks with a broken crest, which is a clear gain over the near-invisible round-1 curtain. Residual: the gain is lopsided. Streaks and a cool-blue lit patch hug the left half of the mouth, while the right half stays as faint as before, so the left side still reads brighter than the right.

vq1b_struct_ruin.png vs the round-1 verify2_struct_ruin: the chunks are warm sooted stone in a loose heap beside the plinth. No cool-grey chunks remain and none reads as a hole. The heap is small and low-contrast at the game camera, so the gain is modest.

vq1_struct_damage66.png: the stage-2 Needle's lower drum and dome are visibly umber-sooted against the clean pale stone of an undamaged tower. The stage read now comes from the material as well as the HP bar. It reads more as an overall brown darkening than as climbing streaks, but it is legible. The ruin stump is dark umber with a pale plinth ring and stays readable.

max2_vq1/rift_core.png and bridge_base.png vs max2_before: there is no perceptible change at the game camera. Frame mean is 82.0 -> 81.6 (core) and 85.3 -> 84.8 (base), std is unchanged, and on the sheet the walked track and kerb drift cannot be found without flicking. The summary itself says it is 'subtle by design'. It is not a regression, but a League-level player will not see it.

1:1 crop of max2_vq1/bridge_deck.png (x 0-700, y 150-800): each bay shows as a faintly paler band edged by two thin dark, slightly wavy lines. They run across the course grid without lining up with its joints. The chalk hour ticks are not visible at 28.5 m, and on bridge_snap there is no visible change under fighters. The deck reads as the same run of courses with two stray seam lines, not as drum bays. Frame mean 66.2 -> 66.3.
ENV-7_slab_recapture.png: no code change this round, and before and after match. Recapture only.

Not built. The reason is recorded in summary.json: at the 52 deg camera they read as floor smears, and the triangle, program and B5 budgets leave no room. I accept the reasoning under the budget margins (seed 11 is at 496.5k of 500k tris, 40 of 40 programs).

problems.what: The clearing floor 'dial-stone slabs and dapple pools' render as hard-rimmed translucent pale ellipses that read as decal stains. The clearings still read as dark moss.
problems.evidence: max2_vq1/rift_jungle_w.png 1:1 crop (two ellipses about x 760-930 and 1300-1480, y 700-860); rift_jungle_s.png around x 700-890, y 380-500
problems.fix: Soften the slab and pool rims into a noise-broken falloff, give the slabs a stone value and seam that read as stone (or drop them), and push the dapple pools warmer and lighter inside the block-top band so the clearing floor actually breaks up.

problems.what: The outflow fall is lopsided: streaks and a cool-blue lit patch on the left half of the mouth, with the right half as faint as round 1
problems.fix: Even the streak density and crest across the full mouth width, and damp the left-side sky or reflection lift so neither bank reads brighter.

problems.what: The BRIDGE deck bays and the base plaza dressing are not perceptible at the gameplay camera. The bays show only as two thin wavy lines that do not line up with the course joints.
problems.evidence: max2_vq1/bridge_deck.png crop x 0-700, y 150-800; rift_core and bridge_base frame stats unchanged (mean within 0.5, std within 0.1)
problems.fix: Line each drum cross-course up with the course joints (straight, on the deck axis), widen the value step of the cross-course, and make the chalk ticks large enough to survive at 28.5 m. For the plaza, either raise the flag-family spread or accept that it is texture noise and drop the claim.

problems.what: Lampbough goes rust-brown in shadow and reads as a withered or autumn tree, while Hourtier reads top-down mostly as a teal recolour of the Dialwood crown
problems.evidence: max2_vq1/rift_jungle_e.png (Lampbough in shade); rift_jungle_w.png centre (Hourtier as a slate blob with a dark trunk hole)
problems.fix: Lift Lampbough's shade colour toward amber (more saturation and a little less value drop under the canopy shadow). Open Hourtier's tier gaps or flatten the top tier so the pagoda silhouette reads from above, and close the dark trunk hole at its crown centre.

problems.what: The triangle margin is 3.5k on the seed 11 match peak (496.5k of 500k), and the match-memory idle reading is still owed
problems.evidence: summary.json gates (the engineer's perf_1080 --prod run; the counts are valid under load). This lane's canopy is -2.5 % tris per tree, so the rise is outside the lane.
problems.fix: Lead: the final idle gate must re-read perf_1080 match counts and probe_match_memory idle before shipping. Any future canopy additions here must pay for themselves.

The engineer's same-order run reports the canopy as triangle-neutral (jungle_e 195k -> 187k). Programs are unchanged at 39 per RIFT spot. Draws rise by 3-6 per RIFT spot (the two new instanced variants), well under 450. Match peak (engineer, perf_1080 --prod --match-only seeds 7/11/23): 451k/496.5k/459k tris, 294/271/289 draws, 40 programs: under every bar, but with only a 3.5k triangle margin. value_probe max2env: 0 FAIL, structure L* p95 RIFT 77.5/79.5 and BRIDGE 75/76.5 (bar <= 80), so B5 holds. I did not re-run perf or the memory probe: the heavy slots were held by perf_1080, value_probe and audio runs from other lanes for over 20 minutes. notes: There is no sensitivity problem: no faces, hoods or horror reads in this lane's assets. Originality: Hourtier (a tiered sage crown), Lampbough (a star-cut quill parasol), the dial-stone slabs, the chalk hour ticks and the sooted Needle are VALE's own and have no LoL counterpart. Nothing is broken. The lane is clearly better than round 1 where it matters most: the jungle, the largest surface on RIFT, now reads as three crown species, and towers carry a damage state in the stone. The rubble and the outflow fall also improved. Three of the eight items (plaza, deck bays, floor break-up) are not visible at the gameplay camera, so the gain is narrower than the summary claims. I score it at par, 7.5, not above. All open problems are minor polish for a round 3.
